rejected.title: Effects of migration on origin and destination
card: The origin is the place migrants leave. The destination is the place they move to. Migration changes both.
Origin
Migrants often send part of their pay home as remittances, which families can spend on food, school fees and housing. The origin can also lose young and skilled workers, such as nurses and engineers.
Destination
Migrants can fill job gaps, such as in farming, building and health care. They also pay taxes and spend money in local shops.
The effects depend on who moves and how many. A place that loses many skilled workers may struggle to run its services.
rejected.remember: Origin: money comes in but workers can leave. Destination: job gaps can be filled.

a.q: Migrants from a village in the Philippines work overseas and send part of their pay to their families. What is this money called?
opts: Remittances
Pull factors
Job gaps
Taxes
a.why: Money that migrants send home to family is called remittances. Pull factors are the things that draw people to a place, so they are not the money itself.
a.clue: Think of money sent back to the origin.

b.q: Many young nurses leave a small town in Ghana for hospitals in another country. Which effect is most likely for the town they left?
opts: Its health services may struggle to find enough staff
Its hospitals may fill with skilled workers from abroad
Its job gaps may be filled by the nurses who left
Its health services may improve with fewer patients
b.why: The origin loses skilled workers, so it can have trouble running services such as health care. Filling job gaps is an effect on the destination, where the nurses now work, not on the town they left.
b.clue: Ask who is leaving, and what the town still needs.
